title: New Media: Target Audience
summary: New media mostly addresses the youth (age group about 12–25) who are computer-savvy and spend more time with computers; with growing competition the youth need to keep informed. Exposure to too much information is information overload, which leaves people confused; difficulty in using so much information causes depression called information fatigue. To prevent it, prioritise information into 'most important', 'important', 'not so important' and 'not required' and develop interest areas. Collecting information does not by itself build logical and analytical powers; raw information without analysis does not add to knowledge.

New media attracts the youth through story telling or narrative writing style, regarded as the most powerful form of communication. It was first used in the USA in the late sixties as 'new journalism' pioneered by Tom Wolfe and is returning with new media. Each story is broken into sections; stories for new media are broken up into several stories which together with multimedia form a package; each story is highlighted on the home page with an attractive visual and a good introductory paragraph; the main story is short and crisp; other stories are in narrative form, preferably human interest stories. New media writers like to do things differently, like Edward de Bono's 'lateral thinking' (he is called the father of creativity).

Parents and teachers worry that children sit before the computer or TV instead of playing outside and chat without meeting friends, so interpersonal skills (talking, listening, sharing, working together) and confidence suffer. Solution: maintain a healthy balance and regulate internet use as television watching is regulated.

New media ventures are not expensive; they can be categorised as small and medium enterprises (SMEs) needing little infrastructure but a lot of creativity. Young people set up small offices and created niche websites (websites with very specialised content such as travel, housing, health, sports); some grew into big companies. E-learning, tourism, property and retail ventures needed a designer, a programmer and freelancers for content. A revenue model is vital: advertising, content selling, subscriptions and specialised services (holiday packages). Online shopping sites and booking of railway and air tickets, ordering dinner, buying books or selling an old car through the internet help busy people.

objective: Fill in the blanks: The stories for new media are broken up into several ______ with ______ to form a package.

Match: (i) Exposure to too much information (ii) Difficulty in using information (iii) New journalism (iv) Father of creativity with (a) Tom Wolfe (b) information overload (c) information fatigue (d) Edward de Bono.
State true or false: (i) We develop interpersonal skills when we deal with people. (ii) Children today are generally found to be socially active.
Fill in the blanks: ______ and ______ are side effects of new media for youth.
Information fatigue; time consumption (or trolling and cyberbullying).
Write the full form of SME and name any one niche website topic.
Small and Medium Enterprises; travel (also housing, health, sports).
vsa: What is meant by information overload?
Exposure to too much information which leaves a person confused and unable to use it.
List any three creative factors of new media that engage youth.
Narrative story telling, stories broken into short segments with multimedia, attractive visuals and short crisp main story, lateral thinking, human interest.
Websites that contain very specialised content such as travel, health or sports.
What is a revenue model in new media?
The way a venture earns income, e.g. advertising, content selling, subscriptions and specialised services.
sa: Explain the impact of new media on youth.
It informs the youth and attracts them with creative narrative stories, but causes information overload and fatigue, reduces outdoor play and interpersonal skills and confidence.
Explain how new media is beneficial for youth with relevant examples.
It gives quick information, online libraries and e-learning, a place to write blogs and chat with friends, online shopping and games and business opportunities.
Discuss the impact of new media on interpersonal relations.
Youth chat online without meeting, so talking, listening and sharing skills and confidence suffer; balance and regulation of internet use are needed.
Is new media a big industry or an SME? Give reasons.
It is an SME as it needs little infrastructure and money but much creativity; niche websites started in small rooms and grew.
la: Discuss the youth as the target audience of new media, with the creativity factor and problems.

The youth spend more time with computers and want information, but face information overload and fatigue; new media attracts them with narrative style, short crisp stories and multimedia, while interpersonal relations suffer.
Explain the business opportunities of new media.
New media ventures are SMEs needing creativity, e.g. niche websites, e-learning, tourism and online shopping, earning through advertising, subscriptions, content selling and services.
